newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch mull quarantine for east Europe pig imports.
newsitem.headline: Dutch mull quarantine for east Europe pig imports.

text.p: The Dutch farm ministry said on Wednesday it was considering quarantine restrictions on imports of pigs from eastern Europe following the discovery of foot-and-mouth disease in six shipments from the region.
A ministry spokesman said the signs of the disease were slight and were probably caused by animals being vaccinated against foot-and-mouth, which is highly contagious among livestock.

"We have found traces of foot-and-mouth in pigs from Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic. The animals have probably been vaccinated against it, which is not allowed in the European Union," he told Reuters.

He said the Dutch government, already struggling to contain an epidemic of swine fever, was working on a policy to hold all further imported live pigs from those countries in quarantine before allowing them through to slaughterhouses.
"The exact contents of the measure are not finalised but we hope to have a quarantine measure in place by the end of the week," the spokesman added.

Swine fever has swelled the number of pigs imported into the Netherlands, with the number of cases growing to almost 280. More than three million pigs have already been destroyed of the country's former 14 million pig population.
Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen has warned that the total number of swine fever cases may top 300 before peaking.
